If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3–5 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment shifts from negative to positive over 3–5 days, accelerate upward correction in mid-horizon (8–15 days) by 1–2% to capture sentiment momentum.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending upward, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid premature bottoming.

If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67) in the last 5 days, apply a 0.5–1.0% smoothing correction across all horizons to dampen erratic forecast swings.
